findings.title: acceptance.node-run@1.1.0 is only a draft, yet the published acceptance.vitest-run@1.0.0 describes itself by reference to it

related.text: acceptance.node-run@1.1.0; a named test absent from the run counts as missing, a code change as stale.

findings.evidence: operation.list returns acceptance.node-run@1.0.0 (source assets/operations/acceptance.node-run.feature) and no 1.1.0. The published description of acceptance.vitest-run@1.0.0 (drafts/acceptance.vitest-run.feature line 7) says it has the same counts, digests and duration as acceptance.node-run@1.1.0. The draft is used by scripts/acceptance-node-run-timed.acceptance.test.mjs line 10, scripts/acceptance-node-repeat.acceptance.test.mjs line 55 and scripts/acceptance-timed-verification.mjs; the unpublished draft acceptance.node-repeat@1.0.0 builds on it. No Procedure invokes acceptance.node-run@1.1.0.
findings.action: The owner publishes acceptance.node-run@1.1.0 from this exact source, then the file moves unchanged to assets/operations/acceptance.node-run-1.1.0.feature and the paths at line 10 of scripts/acceptance-node-run-timed.acceptance.test.mjs and line 55 of scripts/acceptance-node-repeat.acceptance.test.mjs follow.
findings.riskReason: Publishing a version is a product decision and fixes its text for good; the published 1.1.0 must be the draft as it stands. The move itself is safe.

findings.title: The Corpus extension declares no list of the Procedures and Operations it publishes; its README still calls them an example

location.text:
The `procedures` directory contains a reusable example framework and Operations.
Publish under the usual authorized catalog workflow, configure `corpusThreadsUrl`

findings.evidence: Searched extension.json, package.json, build-server.mjs, README.md, IMPLEMENTATION.md and trust-extension/trust-registry.json: the registry index lists only the package relay-gmail (its two Operations and two Procedures carry path, version and sha256); nothing lists Corpus sources. Yet 45 of the 51 Operation and Procedure files under trust-extension/extensions/corpus/procedures (the 52nd file is the vocabulary corpus-terms) are published in the owner's runtime with an identical source, and corpus-thread-framework@0.9.0 drives the engaged framework Plan entretien-code-plan-20261005. Six files are not published: thread-framework.procedure.feature (0.1.0), thread-framework-0.3.0.procedure.feature, thread-read.operation.feature (0.1.0) and the three Procedures of history/ named in another finding. procedure.list shows the Corpus Procedures published by hand (publishedBy local-operator or mcp-agent), while relay-gmail shows publishedBy registry-package:relay-gmail@0.1.0.
findings.action: Add a corpus package to trust-extension/trust-registry.json that lists every published Corpus Operation and Procedure with its path, name, version and sha256, and replace the README paragraph by a pointer to that list.
findings.riskReason: No published source changes, but a registry package becomes installable: each sha256 must match the source already published, or a registry install would conflict with the catalogue; the registry acceptance tests read this index format.
